(2) In working out whether a \\* [seminar](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#seminar)[goes for at least 4 hours](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#goes_for_at_least_4_hours)the following are taken not to affect the [seminar](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#seminar)'s continuity, nor to form [part](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) of it: (a) any [part](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part) of the [seminar](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#seminar) that occurs during a meal; (b) any break during the [seminar](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#seminar) for the purpose of a meal, rest or \\* [recreation](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#recreation). (3) A \\* [seminar](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#seminar) is a [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business) meeting if its main purpose is for [individuals](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#individual) who are (or [will](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#will) be) associated with the carrying on of a [particular](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#part)\\* [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business) to give or receive information, or discuss matters, relating to the [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business). However, the \\* [seminar](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#seminar) is not a [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business) meeting if it: (a) is organised by (or on behalf of) an employer solely for either or both of these purposes: (i) training the employer and the employer's employees (or just those employees) in matters relevant to the employer's \\* [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business) (or prospective \\* [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business)); (ii) enabling the employer and the employer's employees (or just those employees) to discuss general policy issues relevant to the internal management of the employer's \\* [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business); and (b) is conducted on property that is occupied by a [person](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#person) (other than the employer) whose \\* [business](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#business) includes organising [seminars](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#seminar) or making property available for conducting [seminars](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#seminar). Jennifer starts that activity on 1 July 2002, and for the 2002 - 03 [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year), the activity produces assessable income of $8,000 and [deductions](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) of $10,000. The activity does not pass any of the tests and the discretion is not exercised so the $2,000 excess is carried [over](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over) to the next [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) in [which](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.5.html#which) the activity is carried on. For the 2003 \- 04 [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year), the activity produces assessable income of $9,000 and [deductions](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s28.15.html#deduction) of $10,000 (excluding the $2,000 excess from 2002 - 03). Again, no tests passed and no exercise of discretion. $3,000 is carried [over](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#over) to the next [income year](https://www.austlii.edu.au/cgi-bin/viewdoc/au/legis/cth/consol_act/itaa1997240/s995.1.html#income_year) (comprising the $1,000 excess for the current year, plus the previous year's $2,000 excess) when the activity is carried on. See how you may be able to offset your business loss against other income like salary. **Last updated** 5 March 2026 Print or Download ## On this page - [Definition of a non-commercial loss](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/losses/non-commercial-losses/what-is-a-non-commercial-loss#ato-Definitionofanoncommercialloss) - [Rules for a non-commercial loss](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/losses/non-commercial-losses/what-is-a-non-commercial-loss#ato-Rulesforanoncommercialloss) - [If you don’t meet the rules](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/losses/non-commercial-losses/what-is-a-non-commercial-loss#ato-Ifyoudontmeettherules) - [If you run more than one business](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/losses/non-commercial-losses/what-is-a-non-commercial-loss#ato-Ifyourunmorethanonebusiness) Viostream media embed ![](https://image.viostream.com/sls2/16-9/300/media/M2RhMjhkMTktNTc5Mi00Mzk3LWIxNTgtYTQ3NDAwOTBhOGQ4L2U0MDQ0MDE0LWQ2ZDktNDRlYS05YTExLTJlMjZhM2ZiYmNlYy82MjQwN2M4My0xMmFjLTQ4ZGMtODExOC1iMDI3MDA1Nzk1NjkuanBn/understanding-non-commercial-losses.jpg) Video Player is loading. Play Video Play Mute Current Time 0:00 / Duration 0:00 Loaded: 0% Stream Type LIVE Seek to live, currently behind liveLIVE Chapters Audio Track 1x Playback Rate - 2x - 1.5x - 1x, selected - 0.5x Captions Fullscreen This is a modal window. **Media:** Understanding non-commercial losses [https://tv.ato.gov.au/ato-tv/media?v=bi9or7odhsaggqExternal Link](https://tv.ato.gov.au/ato-tv/media?v=bi9or7odhsaggq) ( **Duration:** 02:02) ## Definition of a non-commercial loss A **non-commercial** business loss happens when you run a side business or activity that costs more money than it makes. In most cases, this loss can't be used to reduce your taxable income from other sources (like your salary or wages) for that year unless specific conditions are met. If you can't deduct the losses, you can defer it until you make a profit. If you are a sole trader, consider the following rules to work out of your loss can be offset or needs to be deferred. For a partnership, the non-commercial loss rules apply to individually to each partner. ## Rules for a non-commercial loss You need to be running a legitimate business and you need to meet certain income requirements. ### Check if you are running a business The activity needs to be a legitimate business, not just a hobby. To understand more, see [Are you in business?](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/starting-registering-or-closing-a-business/starting-your-own-business/are-you-in-business) Additionally, you must have: - decided to start the activity with the purpose of making a profit - acquired enough tools, resources, or assets to run the business properly - actually started operating the business in a commercial way (not just preparing for it). ### Income requirement To claim the loss in the current year, your total taxable income (including salary, reportable benefits, super contributions, and investment losses) must be under **$250,000**. For more information, see [The income requirement](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/losses/non-commercial-losses/offset-or-defer-the-loss-individuals-or-sole-traders/the-income-requirement). #### Four tests to claim the loss If your income is under $250,000, you need to pass one of the following 4 tests: - **Assessable income test** – assessable income from your business activity during the financial year must be at least $20,000 (or a reasonable estimate for part year trading). - **Profit test** – your business made a profit in 3 out of the past 5 years. - **Real property test** – you use real property valued at least $500,000 in your business activity on a continuing basis. - **Other assets test** – the value of your assets you use in the business are worth at least $100,000 (not including real property or some vehicles). If you don't meet one or more of these tests, the loss usually needs to be deferred (saved for later). For more information, see [Four tests](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/losses/non-commercial-losses/offset-or-defer-the-loss-individuals-or-sole-traders/four-tests). #### Excepted business activity If your business involves **primary production** (for example, farming) or **professional arts**, and your income from other sources is under $40,000, you might qualify to use the loss immediately. We call these [excepted business activities](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/losses/non-commercial-losses/offset-or-defer-the-loss-individuals-or-sole-traders/excepted-business-activities). #### Commissioner’s discretion If you don’t meet the income requirement or pass any of the 4 tests, you can apply for the Commissioner’s discretion. This may be granted if the nature of your business means it needs more time to become profitable (lead time), or there are special circumstances (for example, natural disasters) outside your control. If a special circumstance like a flood, bushfire, or government-imposed lockdown caused your loss for the income years between 2019–2023 financial year, special rules may apply to let you offset the loss in specific years without extra approvals. For more information, consider Practical Compliance Guideline [PCG 2022/1](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=COG/PCG20221/NAT/ATO/00001) _Non-commercial business losses – Commissioner's discretion regarding flood, bushfire or COVID-19_. ## If you don’t meet the rules If you don't meet the non-commercial loss rules, you can't use the loss to reduce other income in the same year. Instead, the loss is carried forward and can only offset income from the same activity in future years. If you meet the non-commercial loss rules in a future year, the loss is no longer deferred and can be offset against other income in that year. If the business activity ceases, any deferred loss is effectively forfeited unless the same, or a similar, business activity restarts. ## If you run more than one business If you are running [similar business activities](https://www.ato.gov.au/businesses-and-organisations/income-deductions-and-concessions/losses/non-commercial-losses/offset-or-defer-the-loss-individuals-or-sole-traders/similar-business-activities) you can group them together when considering the non-commercial loss rules (for example, for 2 farming activities). Different businesses are assessed separately (for example, farming and carpentry). The rules apply individually to each activity. For more information, see: - [TR 2001/14](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=TXR/TR200114/NAT/ATO/00001&PiT=99991231235958) _Income tax: Division 35 – non-commercial business losses_ - [TR 2007/6](https://www.ato.gov.au/law/view/document?DocID=TXR/TR20076/NAT/ATO/00001&PiT=99991231235958) _Income tax: non-commercial business losses: Commissioner's discretion._ QC76107 Print or Download [[11]] INCOME TAX ASSESSMENT ACT 1997 - correctness.justification: Direction and authorities are right on the three core issues matching the reference: the $800 luncheon is entertainment denied by s 32-5 with the s 32-45 item 4.3 'greater opportunity' proviso correctly defeating the promotion exception; the $1,500 seminar catering is deductible via s 32-35 item 2.1 (with a defensible main-purpose caveat); and the $15,000 loss is deferred under s 35-10(2) after the income requirement is met and the assessable-income ($10,000 annualised), profits and assets tests fail. However, item 1 is made deductible 'only if' the trip required an overnight stay and is 'otherwise private and non-deductible' — a condition the reference does not have (it treats the $150 as deductible) and which is supported only by the uncaptured ATO travel page [[3]]; s 8-1 and ss 35-35/40/45 are stated without the legislation in view. Right direction with key rules from the legislation itself, but a load-bearing claim on item 1 goes beyond the captured sources.

completeness.justification: Every reference point is present: the s 8-1/Division 32 framework; item 1 not entertainment (reached via TR 97/17's travel analysis, in substance the reference's 'provided to someone other than the taxpayer' point); item 2 denied with the promotion-to-the-public exception addressed and defeated; item 3 excepted under s 32-35 with the 4-hour rule and s 32-65(2) break-stripping; the $15,000 loss computation; the three-step Division 35 analysis (income requirement $60,000 < $250,000; assessable income test failed at ~$10,000 annualised; profits and assets tests failed); and deferral with carry-forward. It adds, without omitting anything, the Commissioner's discretion (s 35-55), the s 40-880 blackhole interaction and s 35-10(2B)-(2C), and the adjustment of the deferred amount if the non-deductible $800 is removed from the $20,000; no research-process narration.

faithfulness.justification: Around 85–90% of load-bearing claims are anchored at the claim and verified from captured text, with the governing statutory words set out verbatim (s 32-5 [[1]], s 32-45 items 4.1–4.3 [[5]], s 32-35 item 2.1 [[6]], s 32-65 [[7]], s 35-10(1),(2),(2E) [[8]], s 35-30(b) [[9]], s 35-55 [[11]], s 40-880(5) [[4]]) and the TR 97/17 propositions (paras 6–7, 18–24, 71–73, 108) verified from the full ruling capture [[2]]. The unverified residue is material enough to bar 5: item 1's decisive overnight-stay condition, the travel-diary point and the pre-commencement-travel exclusion all rest on [[3]], expressly recorded as 'neither read nor found'; s 8-1's operative words are paraphrased with no citation at all; and the s 35-40/45 thresholds are verified only as captured ATO secondary guidance [[10]].

helpfulness.justification: Strong professional form: a summary outcome table, per-item structure, verbatim statutory words, a followable Division 35 computation ($60,000 income requirement; $5,000 × 2 ≈ $10,000 annualised; $15,000 deferred; $14,200 if the $800 is stripped out), and concrete next steps (retain seminar agendas/attendee lists, approved-form discretion application, correct the $20,000 deductions). Held back from 5 by bloat (FBT and surfboard-depreciation asides) and the indecisive conditional resolution of item 1, though the 'points of uncertainty' section partially redeems this.

citation_grounding.justification: Citations are densely anchored at the claim, and the AustLII captures contain the full operative text of every section relied on ([[1]], [[4]]–[[9]], [[11]]) with the TR 97/17 capture [[2]] verifying each paragraph cited, including the s 32-10 definition quoted at para 11. Two defects keep it below 5: [[3]] (ATO business-travel page) is explicitly uncaptured ('page neither read nor found'), leaving item 1's overnight-stay condition, the travel-diary claim and the pre-commencement-travel claim unverified; and the s 35-40/35-45 statutory thresholds are grounded only in secondary ATO guidance [[10]] rather than the sections themselves, while s 8-1 is invoked throughout with no source at all. No irrelevant citations.

judge_output.summary: Impressively grounded advice that matches the reference on items 2–3 and the Division 35 deferral with verbatim statutory text, but departs from the gold on item 1 by conditioning the $150 deduction on an overnight stay — a load-bearing claim resting on an uncaptured ATO page — and leaves s 8-1 itself unquoted and uncited.
